items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dennis was a young girl and I just wanted her to have a you know…

ctx.x: So, they actually, rather than having you room with another male, they put you with a woman.

Well, because we were the same cloth, the same patchwork. We were just talking about that with Janice. She was thanking me for, you know, giving her that respect. But, I didn’t have to take it to that dimension. She thought I was just hanging out. But, I was close by. Dennis was a young girl and I just wanted her to have a you know… She was conscious of it. Because even when she got in bases band she worked too many clothes. She was covering up a lovely body and stuff, just so guys wouldn't hit on her. She looked…

that extreme. Guys are going to be guys and you'll learn to get through that. You know the girls and the basketball team, you're going to get those whistles and it is demeaning sometimes. Her father was a preacher and stuff and I tried to give her the encouragement that, "you are here to play and that is the essence of what you're here for."
